A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Ramanujan Library research. All 20 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, support reliable comparison; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original PSLQ and LLL numerical experiments (Figures 3 and 7), measured convergence errors (Table 1), and computationally discovered relations (Section 5 and Appendix F).

after.justification: v2 retains these original numerical experiments, convergence measurements and discovered relations, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The hypergraph representation, PSLQ search, RoI filtering, C-transform calculator, identify procedure and rebounding safeguard remain unchanged (Sections 2–4 and Appendix B).

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mathematical constant families, continued-fraction discovery and identification tasks, and random-vector experiments. The revised example-code footnote does not establish any change in evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The identify comparison with Wolfram Alpha in Section 5 is unchanged. LLL retains the same role as an alternative integer-relation algorithm in Appendix D; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Random-input generation, working precision, tolerance rules, evaluation depths in Table 1, and the search settings in Section 5 are unchanged. Neither version reports a revision to the evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The convergence-error analysis (Table 1), rebounding example (Appendix B/Figure 6), RoI generalization experiment (Appendix D/Figure 7), and identification case study are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Figures 3 and 7 retain the same reporting of 100 runs per condition, averages and standard-deviation error bars. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Both report 118 relations, including 75 considered novel. The plotted outcomes, convergence measurements, identification findings, and relation-specific precision and RoI entries in Appendix F are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, RoI reasoning, Conjectures 1–2, continued-fraction transformations, complexity analysis and proof material in Appendix E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and outlook retain the same claims about the library, hypergraph representation, automated polynomial-relation discovery, 75 novel connections and generalization of Ramanujan’s formula.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the distinction between numerical conjectures and proofs, unresolved convergence proofs, false-positive concerns and the static constant-set limitation. Interpretations of RoI and its applicability also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 footnote 1 replaces a supplementary-code reference and promised future GitHub link with the RamanujanMachine/LIReC repository URL. Footnote 2 replaces the identify.py supplementary-example reference and promised notebook with a specific Colab URL. Implementation and computing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and positioning relative to earlier automated mathematical discovery, Ramanujan Machine, PSLQ and LLL work are unchanged. The added URLs identify the authors’ resources, not additional prior research.

P1.justification: Two explanatory footnotes are replaced with URLs, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The main-body prose, terminology, section order and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter footnotes produce small spacing and pagination shifts on pages 8–10, including moving Figure 4 upward. Figure and table content, captions, labels and overall design remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing future-link placeholders with specific repository and notebook URLs gives readers more actionable resource-access information. This is a limited documentation improvement: the scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged, and the PDFs alone do not establish whether the linked resources are operational.
